description: A complete Introduction to Machine Learning course covering Machine Learning fundamentals, data preprocessing, regression, classification, clustering, decision trees, model evaluation, and real-world applications with practical examples.
subject: Introduction to Machine Learning

prerequisites: Basic data handling with CSV files
Basic understanding of functions and variables

segments.title: Segment 1 – Introduction to ML & Data Preprocessing

modules.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
topics: Meaning and scope of Machine Learning
Data, features, labels and target variables
learningOutcomes: Explain the meaning and scope of Machine Learning
Differentiate major types of Machine Learning
Identify features, labels and target variables
Describe a basic Machine Learning workflow
Identify suitable Machine Learning applications

modules.title: Data Types and Preprocessing
topics: Worked Example 1: Cleaning a student dataset
Worked Example 2: Handling missing salary values
Worked Example 3: Encoding city and gender columns
Worked Example 4: Scaling age and income features
learningOutcomes: Identify common data types used in Machine Learning
Clean datasets by handling missing and inconsistent values
Apply basic feature transformation techniques
Explain the purpose of feature scaling and encoding

modules.title: Feature Selection and Training & Testing Data
topics: Worked Example 1: Selecting features for house price prediction
Worked Example 2: Splitting a student dataset
learningOutcomes: Select suitable features for model building
Separate features and target variables
Create training and testing datasets
Explain the importance of avoiding data leakage

modules.title: Exploratory Data Analysis
topics: Worked Example 1: EDA of student performance data
Worked Example 2: EDA of house prices
Worked Example 3: Detecting an outlier using a box plot
learningOutcomes: Summarize a dataset using basic statistics
Create and interpret common EDA visualisations
Identify patterns, relationships and possible outliers

modules.title: Simple Linear Regression
topics: Worked Example 1: Salary prediction from experience
Worked Example 2: House price prediction from area
Worked Example 3: Sales prediction from advertising expenditure
Worked Example 4: Marks prediction from study hours
learningOutcomes: Explain simple linear regression
Fit a basic regression model
Predict values using a regression equation
Interpret slope, intercept and residuals

modules.title: Multiple Linear Regression
topics: Worked Example 1: House price using area and bedrooms
Worked Example 2: Sales using multiple advertising channels
Worked Example 3: Student marks using study hours and attendance
learningOutcomes: Explain multiple linear regression
Use multiple features for prediction
Interpret regression coefficients
Recognize the basic effect of correlated predictors

modules.title: Regression Model Evaluation
topics: Comparison of MAE, MSE and RMSE
Worked Example 4: Comparing two regression models
learningOutcomes: Calculate MAE, MSE and RMSE
Interpret regression evaluation results
Compare regression models using suitable metrics

modules.title: Regression Applications and Practice
topics: Worked Example 1: Complete house price prediction
Worked Example 2: Complete student marks prediction
learningOutcomes: Apply the complete regression workflow
Interpret predictions and evaluation metrics
Identify basic limitations of linear regression

modules.title: Logistic Regression
learningOutcomes: Explain Logistic Regression for classification
Interpret probability-based predictions
Build a basic binary classifier

modules.title: K-Nearest Neighbours (KNN)
topics: Effect of feature scaling on KNN
Worked Example 3: KNN with different values of K
learningOutcomes: Explain the KNN algorithm
Calculate basic distances for KNN
Choose a suitable K value
Recognize the importance of feature scaling

modules.title: Naive Bayes Classifier
topics: Worked Example 1: Simple categorical Naive Bayes
Worked Example 3: Small student classification problem
learningOutcomes: Explain the basic idea of Naive Bayes
Apply Bayes theorem to simple classification problems
Interpret prior, likelihood and posterior probabilities

modules.title: Classification Model Evaluation
topics: Worked Example 1: Constructing a confusion matrix
Worked Example 6: Comparing Logistic Regression and KNN
learningOutcomes: Construct and interpret a confusion matrix
Calculate accuracy, precision and recall
Calculate and interpret F1-score
Select suitable classification metrics

modules.title: K-Means Clustering
topics: Choosing the number of clusters K
learningOutcomes: Explain the purpose of clustering
Apply the basic K-Means procedure
Interpret centroids and clusters
Use a simple method for selecting K

modules.title: Decision Tree Concept and Structure

Worked Example 2: Loan approval decision tree
Worked Example 3: Simple product classification tree

Worked Example 2: Information gain for a feature

Select a suitable split using information gain

modules.title: Decision Tree Model Building and Interpretation
topics: Worked Example 1: Complete student prediction model
Worked Example 3: Comparing shallow and deep trees

modules.title: Model Validation

Worked Example 2: Comparing training and testing accuracy

Compare training and testing performance

modules.title: Model Comparison and Selection
topics: Worked Example 1: Comparing Logistic Regression and KNN
Worked Example 3: Selecting the best model using cross-validation

Worked Example 3: Customer segmentation case study

Coding Exercise 2: Train and evaluate a classifier
learningOutcomes: Explain the roles of TensorFlow and Keras
Build a basic neural network model

modules.title: Signal Processing Fundamentals

modules.title: Impulse Function and Ramp Function
learningOutcomes: Define the impulse function

courseOutcomes.description: Explain the basic concepts, types, and applications of machine learning in data-driven problem solving.
Prepare datasets through preprocessing, feature selection, and data transformation for model building.
Apply fundamental machine learning algorithms for regression, classification, and clustering tasks.
Evaluate and interpret the performance of machine learning models using appropriate metrics.
Use suitable tools and libraries to implement simple machine learning solutions on real datasets.

assessment.type: Concepts + Numerical Problems + Coding Exercises + Module Tests + Mini Project

textBooks: Machine Learning using Python, Manaranjan Pradhan & U. Dinesh Kumar, Wiley India (2019; also 2nd edition 2025).
Machine Learning with Python, Abhishek Vijayvargia, BPB Publications (2018).
Applied Machine Learning Solutions with Python, Siddhanta Bhatta, BPB Publications (2022).
Introduction to Machine Learning with Python: A Guide for Data Scientists, Andreas C. Müller & Sarah Guido, Shroff Publishers (2016).
Data Science and Machine Learning Using Python, Reema Thareja, McGraw Hill India.

extendedCourseOutcomes.description: Apply advanced clustering and classification algorithms including K-Medoids, Hierarchical Clustering, Density-Based Clustering, Perceptron, and Support Vector Machines.
Explain regularized and probabilistic machine learning methods including Polynomial Regression, Ridge, Lasso, SVM, and Relevance Vector Machine.
Explain and implement fundamental Deep Learning concepts including activation functions, gradient descent, neural networks, multilayer perceptrons, backpropagation, TensorFlow, and Keras.
Apply basic signal processing and convolutional neural network concepts including FFT, CNNs, impulse functions, and ramp functions.

roadmapExtension.purpose: Extend the original five segments to cover the additional topics present in the supplied university Machine Learning syllabus.
roadmapExtension.note: The original five segments and their contents are preserved. The additional 24 hours represent the newly added syllabus coverage and are an extension of the learning roadmap, not a replacement of the original 45-hour allocation.
